home.aboutText: Kukljica is a picturesque tourist and fishing village, located at the southeastern tip of the island of Ugljan, adjacent to the neighboring island of Pašman. The diversity of tourist offerings, the beauty of the landscape characterized by dense pine forests, sandy and rocky beaches on the shores of crystal clear sea, an equipped harbor in a sheltered natural cove, and a wide selection of accommodation in private apartments and rooms, and Holiday Park Zelena Punta, provide opportunities for an ideal holiday.

about.title: About us
about.heroSubtitle: Visit us and feel the beauty of Kukljica
about.introText: The Municipality of Kukljica is a small tourist and fishing village on the island of Ugljan, with its first known written record from 1106. In addition to the settlement itself, it includes four small islands: Bisage, Golac, Mišnjak and Karantunić.
about.howToGetText: Kukljica is located on the island of Ugljan and is easily accessible by ferry or boat from Zadar. From the Gaženica port to Preko, the journey takes about 25 minutes, and from there you are 10 minutes away from Kukljica by car, bicycle or local transport. Passengers without vehicles can also use fast boat lines. If you are coming by car, follow the signs to Gaženica, and upon arriving on the island, continue along the local road. Zadar Airport is only 15 minutes drive from the ferry port.

howToGet.title: How to get here?
howToGet.introText:
Kukljica is located on the island of Ugljan and is easily accessible by ferry or boat from Zadar. From the Gaženica port to Preko, the journey takes about 25 minutes, and from there you are 10 minutes away from Kukljica by car, bicycle or local transport.

If you are coming by car, follow the signs to Gaženica. Zadar Airport is only 15 minutes drive from the ferry port, making Kukljica easily accessible by air as well.
howToGet.carText: By road and ferry via Preko on the island of Ugljan, Kukljica is connected to Zadar. From Austria and Hungary via Zagreb, Zadar or Biograd. From Italy via Rijeka, Zadar or Biograd. Preko - Kukljica 5 km, Kukljica - Tkon 25 km.
howToGet.boatText: By boat to Zadar, then by ferry via Preko on the island of Ugljan.
howToGet.trainText: From all European destinations via Zagreb to the Zadar railway station, then by ferry to Preko or Tkon and by bus to Kukljica.
howToGet.planeText: From all destinations worldwide via Zagreb and Split or directly to Zadar Zemunik airport, then by ferry to Preko or Tkon and by car/bus to Kukljica.
howToGet.busText: Public transport is organized by buses to all major places on the island.

landmarks.title: Landmarks
landmarks.heroSubtitle: Discover the cultural heritage of Kukljica
landmarks.writtenRecordText:
The name Kukljica is first mentioned in written sources in 1106, in a document published in the Codex diplomaticus by Tadija Smičiklas. The document mentions the donation of an olive grove to the Zadar monastery of St. Chrysogonus, marking Kukljica's entry into historical records.

Among the more significant buildings, although unfortunately damaged, are the castle (summer residence) of the Nassi family from 1623 and the remains of an unknown building in Ortulan's court.
landmarks.churchGospe: Church of Our Lady of the Snow
landmarks.churchGospeText:
The Church of Our Lady of the Snow is located in the Ždrelac sea strait, between the islands of Ugljan and Pašman. The feast of the church's patron saint is celebrated every year on August 5th, continuously since 1514.

The interior is adorned with the main altar with four marble columns, and the church has five altars in total. The church reflects the Baroque style of the 17th century and represents a valuable cultural monument. It has been under state protection since 1982.
landmarks.churchJeronimText:
The Church of St. Jerome is located northwest of Kukljica, in the quiet cove of Kostanj, with a view of the Zadar channel. Historians date it to the 14th century, but by the end of the 16th century it was abandoned and left to decay.

Thanks to donations and contributions from Kukljica residents, the church has been thoroughly renovated. Extensive restoration and conservation work was carried out.
landmarks.churchPavaoText:
In the very center of the village is the parish church dedicated to the Conversion of St. Paul. On that site once stood a late Roman or early Croatian chapel, demolished and rebuilt from the foundations in 1666.

The current church bears the characteristics of the 17th century Baroque style. The interior houses the main altar dedicated to the Blessed Lady of Carmel.

beaches.title: Beaches
beaches.heroSubtitle: Discover the hidden gems of the Adriatic
beaches.sabusaText: Sabuša beach is located on the western coast of the island, about 20 minutes walk from the center of Kukljica. The sea here is shallow and sandy, making the beach ideal for families with young children. Concrete sections are perfect for sunbathing, while natural shade provides a pleasant refuge from the sun.
beaches.jelenicaText: Jelenica beach is a naturist beach located near Sabuša cove, surrounded by centuries-old olive trees that provide natural shade and tranquility. It can be reached by a leisurely walk, about 25 minutes from the center of Kukljica. The beach is a combination of sand and pebbles.
beaches.kostanjText: Kostanj beach is located north of Kukljica, in a quiet cove surrounded by dense pine forest. The sandy shore and pristine natural setting make it an ideal place for relaxation away from the crowds. The cove is also suitable for anchoring smaller boats.
beaches.zelenaPuntaText: The Holiday Park Zelena Punta beach is located in the immediate vicinity of the accommodation complex, surrounded by pine forest that provides natural shade and peace. The beach is partly concrete and partly pebbly, with easy access to the sea.

activeVacation.title: Active Vacation
activeVacation.heroSubtitle: Discover active moments you can experience in Kukljica
activeVacation.hikingText: The Lungomare trails are ideal for leisurely walks along the coast, through coves and centuries-old pine forests. The interior of the island is connected to Kukljica by hiking trails through olive groves and pine forests. For those seeking a challenge, there are more demanding mountain trails with viewpoints offering spectacular views of the Zadar archipelago.
activeVacation.cyclingText: Cycling enthusiasts can rent bicycles within Holiday Park Zelena Punta and enjoy relaxed rides through the beautiful island landscapes. Whether you're looking for light recreation or an active tour of hidden corners, cycling is the perfect way to explore.
activeVacation.nauticsText: For an authentic and unforgettable experience of Kukljica, we recommend renting a boat to discover hidden coves and beaches inaccessible by land. Only from the sea does the island reveal its most beautiful, unspoiled parts.
activeVacation.tripsText: Hidden coves and nearby islets such as Mišnjak, Iž, Sestrunj, Rivanj and Dugi otok offer numerous opportunities for day boat trips. Panoramic tours are organized for sea and underwater enthusiasts, with numerous excursion boats with experienced hosts.

nautika.title: Nautics
nautika.heroSubtitle: Explore the beauty of Kukljica and its coastline by boat
nautika.section1Text:
Kukljica is the ideal starting point for exploring Telašćica Nature Park and Kornati National Park. Located along the Ždrelac passage and Ždrelašćica cove (44°N, 15°15' E), it offers a perfect location for sailors.

Kukljica's harbor is modern, naturally protected and has about 100 berths. Nearby marinas in Zadar, Biograd and on the island of Iž are all within an hour's sailing.
nautika.section2Text:
Kukljica and Ždrelašćica rank among the most favorable nautical locations in Croatia. In addition to the excellent position in the most indented part of the Adriatic, the place lies on the main nautical routes towards Kornati and Dugi Otok.

The harbor is located in the center of the village, providing quick access to all amenities.

cycling.title: Cycling
cycling.heroSubtitle: For those who prefer to explore on two wheels
cycling.section1Text: The island is ideal for cycling – whether you pedal along the quiet coast, through the shade of pine forests or charming island villages, each route offers a unique experience of nature and Mediterranean ambience. Regardless of fitness level, everyone can find an ideal route.
cycling.section2Text: Bicycles are available for rent at Holiday Park Zelena Punta, where your island adventure on two wheels begins. Explore pristine nature, hidden coves and enjoy the views from beautiful lookout points throughout the island.
cycling.rentText: Contact us to rent a bicycle.

hiking.title: Hiking
hiking.heroSubtitle: Hiking in clean, salty air is ideal for health and relaxation in nature
hiking.section1Text: The Lungomare trails are suitable for all walkers and follow the coast through picturesque coves and centuries-old pine forests. The other side of the island is connected to Kukljica by gentle trails through olive groves and the quiet interior. For more experienced walkers there are more demanding trails that reward with magnificent views of the Zadar archipelago.
hiking.trail6: Trail 6 — Kukljica – Veli vrh (122 m) – Nehaj – Kali | 5.5 km | 2 hours | Easy
hiking.trail16: Trail 16 — Kukljica – Ilovača – Nehaj – Sv. Pelegrin – Kali | 5 km | 1 h 30 min | Easy
hiking.trail17: Trail 17 — Kukljica – Sv. Jerolim – Otrić – Kali | 5 km | 1 h 20 min | Tourist trail
hiking.trail19: Trail 19 — Kukljica – Jelenica cove – Sabuša cove – Gospa Snježna – Glavina cape – Kukljica | 6.5 km | 1 h 40 min | Tourist trail

trips.title: Trips
trips.section1Text:
Numerous hidden coves around Kukljica provide perfect opportunities for day boat trips. You can sail to nearby islets like Mišnjak or explore the neighboring islands of the Zadar archipelago – Iž, Sestrunj, Rivanj and Dugi otok.

Panoramic tours are organized for sea and underwater enthusiasts, with numerous excursion boats with experienced hosts. All information is available at the tourist board office, at the Holiday Park Zelena Punta reception, or directly on the boats.
trips.section2Text: Kukljica's location enables numerous excursions, both along the coast and into its hinterland. Within 100 to 150 kilometers there are beautiful islands, historic cities, and nature parks Velebit and Vransko jezero, as well as national parks Paklenica, Krka and Plitvice Lakes.
trips.infoText: Find out more about trips around Kukljica

zelenaPunta.title: Holiday Park Zelena Punta
zelenaPunta.quote: My family and I got newly renovated apartment, with an amazing view on pine trees, the sea and mount Velebit in the distance. The smell in the morning returned me to my childhood because of the untouched Mediterranean vegetation. Very nice and calming surrounding, all green and blue.
zelenaPunta.section1Text:
Kukljica is a picturesque tourist and fishing village on the southeast of the island of Ugljan, near the island of Pašman. It is characterized by dense pine forests, sandy and rocky beaches by crystal clear sea and an equipped harbor in a natural cove. Accommodation is available in private apartments and rooms and in Holiday Park Zelena Punta.

It is also called the "gateway to Telašćica Nature Park and NP Kornati" due to its proximity to the Ždrelac passage.
zelenaPunta.section2Text:
Thanks to excellent connections with the mainland, mild climate, clean sea, proximity to Zadar, national parks and cultural events, Kukljica is an important island destination of the Zadar region.

A special attraction is the traditional boat procession on August 5th, which since 1514 carries the statue of Our Lady of the Snow from Ždrelašćica cove to the parish church of St. Paul. In summer, exhibitions, concerts, theatrical and poetry evenings, festivals and many other events are held.
